REV-1 [R9] The disk mutation and the editor-store update are not atomic, so a persist failure leaves a half-applied operation: the item is renamed/moved/deleted on disk (the reloaded tree shows the new state) while the command returns 'could not be renamed/moved/deleted' and the open tab still points at the old path (or a deleted file). That breaks R9's pitfall 'the tab must be re-pointed to the new path as part of the same operation, so a tab never points at a file that no longer exists' and 'a failed operation must not leave a half-created or half-moved item behind'.

REV-2 [USR-003] The row selection is not invalidated after an operation. Move (which has no confirmation prompt) will then silently move whatever file now sits at the stale old path: e.g. rename a.txt -> b.txt, create a new a.txt, then press Move/Delete on the invisible stale selection and the new a.txt is acted on instead of the item the user sees.

REV-3 [USR-003] Duplicated path-normalisation logic (USR-003 code duplication / USR-006 'reuse before reinventing') should be centralised, for example next to parentFolder in src/features/explorer/root.ts, so the component comparison cannot drift between the hooks.

QA-1 [R9] R9 acceptance 'the deleted item is in the Recycle Bin and can be restored from there' is unproven: no test distinguishes binning from permanent deletion. Add a test that finds the item in the Recycle Bin (e.g. `trash::os_limited::list()`) or restores it; an assertion that the path is gone is not enough.

QA-2 [R11] R11 acceptance 'Start all leaves non-executable terminals stopped and starts the executable ones' and edge 'Stop all does not stop a non-executable terminal the user started by hand' are unproven at the command. The same start_all is used by the launch-time restore (useLauncher.ts:299), so that acceptance is also unproven. Add a command-level test that proves the filters at commands.rs:137/:161, not only the helper.

QA-3 [R9] R9 edge 'a move between different drives cannot be a plain rename; it is reported as a clear error and the original stays where it was' is proven only at helper level. A real second volume is needed, so this is advisory, but the guard in move_item itself is unproven.
QA-4 [R9] R9 edge 'renaming or moving a file that has unsaved text keeps the unsaved text in the tab and only changes the path' is only proven for rename. Add the same snapshot assertion for a move.

QA-5 [R11] R11 acceptance 'a non-executable terminal's own Start and Stop controls still start and stop it' and edge 'marking a running terminal non-executable does not by itself stop it' are only thinly proven. Assert the handlers fire for a non-executable terminal, and that saving the flag off on a running terminal does not call stop.
QA-6 [R12] R12 edge 'Ctrl+R is not assigned to refresh and stays available to the shell' should be asserted directly (`matchShortcut`/`isAppShortcut` for Ctrl+R is null/false).
QA-7 [R9] R9 acceptance 'tab groups are recomputed' is only covered indirectly by the path update. Add an assertion that a tab moves between app groups (or into/out of Misc) after rename or move.

QA-8 [R9] The R9 non-functional performance check ('in a folder with 1,000 entries, creating or renaming one item refreshes that level and stays usable, and no unrelated folder is re-read') is not exercised as a single scenario, only as separate truncation and reloadFolder tests.

QA-9 [R9] The R9 non-functional accessibility check ('using only the keyboard, a user can create, rename, move and delete an item, seeing the focus at each step') has no test, even though the controls are native buttons and a non-drag Move action exists.
